payload.claim: Criterion 2 requires that when `runtime.remove_container(container)` exits non-zero inside the fallback, no ephemeral container is started, the one failure line names the removal's stderr, and the container's name stays in `created`. No test in tests/test_session.py ever makes the fallback's own `remove_container` call return non-zero: `_stub_export_network`'s `_remove_container` always returns `Completed(0, "", "")`, and the one test that does vary `remove_container`'s outcome (`test_a_container_the_export_removed_is_not_reported_surviving_teardown`) makes the first two calls (the pre-clean and the export's own) succeed, only failing the third (`cell_down`'s). Deleting the `if removed.returncode != 0: ...; return None, subjects` guard entirely (so the code unconditionally does `created.discard(container)` and proceeds to allocate the network and read the volume regardless of whether the removal actually succeeded) keeps every existing test green, since none of them exercises a failing removal in this call site, yet it violates exactly the behavior criterion 2 claims is witnessed, and the gate table reports `criteria: pass`.
